idle: (He checks his pocket watch.) On time. For now.
good_ice: Good ice, on time. A dispatcher's dream.
bad_ice: Bad ice means long whistles means delays. I can feel the timetable slipping.
wet_ice: Flood ran long. We are now four minutes behind. Four.
cold: Cold is fine. Cold is punctual.
hungry: Lunch is 12:15. I'll be eating at 12:15. Thereabouts. No. 12:15.
long_line: This queue is a bottleneck. In freight, we'd add a siding.
goal: Goal at 14:32. Noted on the sheet.
greet_owner: Good morning. You're on time. I noticed.
Ah. The owner. Arriving on schedule.
leaving_happy: Every game on time. I'm going to sit in the car and enjoy it.
leaving_angry: Forty minutes behind. Roughly. I hate that I had to say roughly.

tournament: Game six departs at 13:15! Zamboni clears the platform at 13:05!
Coaches, your seventy-five minutes start now.
minor_hockey: The grandkids are on at nine. I'm here at 8:20. Of course I am.

first.say: Bob Ferreira. Thirty-four years dispatching freight out of Carrick Junction. I chair the Valley Peewee Tournament committee. A game every seventy-five minutes, a flood between. You'll be the owner.

options.text: We'll run it to the minute, Bob.

first_minute.say: (He checks his watch, then you.) Good. I'll hold you to it. Not unkindly. Precisely.

first_roughly.say: Roughly. (He winces.) Roughly is the word that derailed the 7:40 to Kessler in 1989. We'll talk.

first_watch.say: My father's. Railway grade. It's lost nine seconds since 1961. I've forgiven it.

options.text: I'm sorry, Bob. It won't happen again.

say: Game four departs at 10:45. Not 10:46. (He taps the schedule board.) We're on time. For now.
Flood in six minutes. Then game five. Then lunch. Then the crest table. Then game six.

options.text: I'll leave you to the schedule.

promise_kept.say: You said to the minute. The last game left at 18:15. Not 18:16. In thirty-four years of freight I never once had a weekend like it.

say: Good morning. What can I schedule for you?

options.text: How does the rink do on a tournament weekend?
What's the secret to running on time?

job.say: Thirty-four years at Carrick Junction. Eighty cars a day, two main lines and one siding with a temper. I retired to be near the grandkids. Now I dispatch peewees.

events.say: A tournament is a railway with skates. Teams from five towns, a game every seventy-five minutes, a flood between. When it runs on time it's the most beautiful thing in the valley.

events_crest.say: Tommy Bellweather runs it. Eleven years old and a better trader than any dispatcher I knew. He got a Wendover crest for a Millbrook pin and a cough drop.

gossip.say: Donna Pettigrew is the best organiser I've worked with, and I worked for the railway. Larry Piche keeps the clock. And Lorraine at the Hot Stove makes the Legion's chili, which runs on its own schedule.

rink.say: The floods are the bottleneck. Ten minutes is a flood. Fourteen minutes is a delay. Twenty is a derailment.

rink_better.say: Ten minutes, every flood. Earl and Doris run like the 6:05. I told him so. He said 'Doris doesn't run, she glides'. Fair.

schedule.say: Edge the boards before the weekend, flood between every game and never let overtime happen. Overtime is chaos with a scoreboard.
